newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed mixed with a slightly lower bias as the market consolidated after hitting new all-time highs earlier this week.
The AEX index of 25 blue chip stocks closed 0.74 points or 0.13 percent lower at 589.74 after closing above 590 for the first time on Tuesday.
Dealers said prices seemed set to follow a sideways pattern in the short term with options market-makers apparently keen to see the AEX around 590 for tomorrow afternoon's October expiry.
"We saw some profit-taking today, but the options exchange pushed the index back up when it fell much below 590," said one.
Some dealers believe the market might face a downward correction in the slightly longer term.
One dealer cited bearish chart signals in support of this view noting that the AEX chart had showed several Doji candlestick formations this month.
A Doji is formed when a market or instrument opens and closes at the same levels. Chartists usually interpret this as signalling a turning point.
Dojis occurred on October 9 and 15 and, arguably, again on Thursday.
In the absence of news from major firms, two small ones -- Artu Biologicals and Toolex Alpha -- provided the main focus.

Biotech firm Artu kept up its two-week winning streak in heavier than usual trading activity, gaining 1.50 at 10.50 guilders. Some dealers said private investors had been buying the shares after a Dutch investment magazine tipped them.

Toolex Alpha, a Swedish-based CD production systems maker, fell 8.80 to 23.60 after it warned of a slowdown in orders. The bourse cancelled all trades in the shares before 1330 GMT, citing "inequality of information" ahead of the warning.
